simple.meaning: יְרֻשָּׁה (yᵉrushshâh) is a Hebrew object word meaning “something occupied ; a conquest ; also a patrimony.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Deuteronomy 2:5. The surrounding context includes family, land, Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to יְרֻשָּׁה (H3425) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: יְרֻשָּׁה (yᵉrushshâh) / H3425 is traced through Deuteronomy 2:5, Deuteronomy 2:9, Deuteronomy 2:12, Deuteronomy 2:19 with generated occurrence evidence.

definitions.short: something occupied ; a conquest ; also a patrimony
definitions.full: H3425. yerushshah יְרֻשָּׁה noun feminine (a) possession, inheritance ; — absolute ׳יר Deut 2:5 7 t., construct יְרֻשַּׁת Judg 21:17 ; Psa 61:6 (but on text see below); suffix יְרֻשָּֽׁתְךָ 2Chr 20:11 ; יְרֻשָּׁתוֺ Deut 2:12 ; 3:20 ; יְרֻשַּׁתְכֶם Josh 1:15 ; — used of land Deut 2:5 , 9 (twice in verse); 2:19 (twice in verse); 3:20 ; יְרֻשָּׁתוֺ אֶרֶץ 2:12 the land of his possession , so Josh 1:15 ; further, 12:6-7 , Judg 21:7 (but Bu Rs 152 נִשְׁאֲרָה ), Jer 32:8 + Jer 61:6 (but < אֲרֶשֶׁת request , compare Che critical note .), 2Chr 20:11 .
